Tidyups Cleaning assured Richard that his cleaners do not try to extend their time unnecessarily and are honest about their work. Richard mentioned he used to work with cleaners frequently in leasing and is interested in establishing an ongoing cleaning arrangement. Richard requested a quote for cleaning services four times a month and two times a month for the same property.

callTranscripts.summary: Richard was billed for four hours, but he claims the cleaners were only there for about an hour and a half. Richard expressed concern about being charged for time not worked and stated he prefers fairness in billing. Tidyups Cleaning acknowledged the misunderstanding and agreed to adjust the invoice from $240 to $180 for an hour and a half of work. Richard confirmed the cleaners arrived at 02:26 PM and left at 04:31 PM. Tidyups Cleaning assured Richard that his cleaners do not try to extend their time unnecessarily and are honest about their work. Richard mentioned he used to work with cleaners frequently in leasing and is interested in establishing an ongoing cleaning arrangement. Richard requested a quote for cleaning services four times a month and two times a month for the same property.

callTranscripts.summary: Richard was billed for four hours, but he claims the cleaners were only there for about an hour and a half. Richard expressed concern about being charged for time not worked and stated he prefers fairness in billing. Tidyups Cleaning acknowledged the misunderstanding and agreed to adjust the invoice from $240 to $180 for an hour and a half of work. Richard confirmed the cleaners arrived at 02:26 PM and left at 04:31 PM. Tidyups Cleaning assured Richard that his cleaners do not try to extend their time unnecessarily and are honest about their work. Richard mentioned he used to work with cleaners frequently in leasing and is interested in establishing an ongoing cleaning arrangement. Richard requested a quote for cleaning services four times a month and two times a month for the same property.

I’m genuinely confused by this marketing strategy. I accidentally clicked on one of your ads, which caused your business to message me first. I did not reach out to you.

I then asked whether you even service Eastern Nova Scotia, and instead of answering that question, your automated system thanked me for “reaching out” and sent me a booking link and an Alberta phone number.

If you don’t even service my part of Canada, why are your ads being shown here and automatically opening business chats with people who click them?

Clicking an advertisement is not the same thing as contacting a business or requesting a quote. If you’re going to use automated messaging, the very least it could do is recognize the difference between a customer contacting you and your advertising system contacting them.

Nothing makes me want to hire a cleaning company quite like being solicited by one that apparently can’t even clean in my province. 🙃

I would seriously consider reviewing how this automated system is set up, because I can very easily see it costing your business potential customers and eventually resulting in negative reviews. Unsolicited automated messages after someone simply clicks on an advertisement are frustrating enough, but it becomes even more frustrating when the advertisement is being shown to people who aren’t even remotely within your service area.

Clicking on an ad — especially accidentally — should not be treated as though someone has personally contacted your business, requested a quote, or given permission to be solicited. In my case, I asked a very straightforward question about whether you service Eastern Nova Scotia, and instead of receiving an answer, I was immediately directed to a booking page and given an Alberta phone number.

Businesses really need to understand how irritating this type of automated marketing is becoming for customers. Trying to turn every accidental ad click into a sales lead doesn’t create a positive customer experience — it feels intrusive and forced. And when the person being contacted isn’t even in the province or anywhere remotely near the area you service, it makes even less sense.

I’m saying this as constructive feedback because this kind of system can create a negative impression of an otherwise perfectly good business before a potential customer has even had a real interaction with anyone from the company.
